title: Full Stack Developer
card_description: Pre-filled with optimized power words for both frontend and backend engineering, matching top ATS requirements.
description: Our research team analyzed fifty junior full-stack resumes. Most of them get rejected immediately because candidates just list out 15 different frameworks without explaining how they connect. We built this template to fix that.
core_philosophy: Our philosophy is simple: show the architecture. Don't just give a shopping list of tools. This layout is designed to help you explain exactly how you separated your frontend View from your backend Controller.
personal_story: During our industry research, we interviewed several recruiters and found a common pattern. A candidate whose resume just lists 'React' and 'Node.js' gets ignored. But a candidate who explicitly writes out how their project's API was too slow, and exactly how they implemented Redis to fix the load times, gets the interview. Recruiters want to see the problems you hit and how you handled them.
ats_optimizations: We made sure this template forces you to use the exact keywords our HR software scans for, like JSON Web Tokens and RESTful APIs.
We put the Academic Projects section at the very top. This is a neat trick our team learned to hide the fact that you don't have professional experience yet.
We formatted the GitHub links so that our recruiter's automated scraper grabs your portfolio data instantly.
We changed all the phrasing. Instead of saying 'Developed an app', this template makes you say 'Architected a full-stack CRUD application', because that's how we talk on the job.

title: Data Analyst
card_description: Packed with actionable verbs and data translation keywords designed strictly to bypass initial automated screenings.
description: When our team researched hiring patterns for data analysts, we found that employers don't care if you just know how to open Tableau. They care if your data can stop the company from losing money. We designed this template to focus on ROI.
core_philosophy: A major red flag for recruiters is listing 'SQL' as a skill without context. This format forces you to tie your SQL queries directly to a business outcome. If your project doesn't show measurable impact, HR filters will drop it.
personal_story: We analyzed dozens of successful data analyst interviews and discovered a recurring theme. Interviewers rarely quiz candidates on Python syntax. Instead, they point to a bullet point about 'cleaning data' and ask, 'So what?' The candidates who get hired are the ones who can explain how their data project could actually help a business identify high-risk customers before they churn.
ats_optimizations: We specifically added SQL join types (like INNER and LEFT) into the bullet points because I know our system filters out resumes without them.
We organized the tools into Visualization, Database, and Scripting sections so the robotic parsers don't get confused.
We made sure every bullet point requires a measurable impact figure (like 'reduced time by 20%') instead of vague responsibilities.
We included A/B testing methodologies because marketing teams are begging for that skill right now, and no one puts it on their resume.

title: Data Engineer
card_description: Features optimal vocabulary for ETL pipelines, big data integration, and data warehousing to stand out to recruiter AIs.
description: Employers don't need Data Engineers to build pretty dashboards. They need to know your ETL pipeline won't fail under heavy load. We put this layout together to help you showcase your deep-level infrastructure skills.
core_philosophy: In data engineering, reliability is everything. We stripped all the UI/UX fluff out of this template. It focuses entirely on batch processing algorithms and how you move data securely. That proves you aren't a liability.
personal_story: Our research into Senior Data Architect roles revealed a massive secret: successful candidates talk about failures. Instead of just listing tools, they detail a time their raw log pipeline crashed under massive load, and the exact steps they took to orchestrate a fix using Apache Airflow. Hiring managers want to see that you've been in the trenches and survived.
ats_optimizations: We added cloud-native terms like Data Lakes and Serverless Computing so you can bypass the strict enterprise IT scanners.
We formatted the skills section to put Python directly next to your data frameworks, so the parsing bots link the two concepts together.
We styled the academic project section to look exactly like real-world enterprise infrastructure builds.
We completely removed non-relevant keywords to keep your keyword density 100% focused on backend data integration.

title: Software Engineer
card_description: Standardized, cleanly formatted generic engineering templates filled with algorithmic problem-solving and SDLC buzzwords.
description: Our team analyzed hundreds of automated ATS parsers. Complex layouts with crazy colors or progress bars instantly break the parser. We created this ultra-clean template to focus purely on your core computer science logic.
core_philosophy: A software engineer's resume should be as clean as their code. This format isolates your algorithmic problem-solving and forces you to explain the time complexity of your projects, proving you actually understand what you're doing.
personal_story: We interviewed several elite backend managers to find out how they shortlist candidates. They told us they ignore resumes that just say 'Built a chat app.' They only shortlist candidates who dedicate bullet points to explaining real engineering bottlenecks—like how a server had massive memory leaks during user spikes, and how the candidate refactored the threading model to fix it.
ats_optimizations: We removed every single image and complex table to ensure a perfect parse rate on legacy systems like Workday.
We separated your programming languages from your software environments to make it easier for our initial bot scan.
We built unit testing and debugging skills natively into the academic bullet points.
We added specific phrasing around memory management to prove you have fundamental computer science competency.

title: Data Scientist
card_description: Highlight your statistical modeling, machine learning, and data visualization expertise using verified industry phrasing.
description: The data science field is flooded with people who just run a basic linear regression script and call themselves experts. We designed this template to force you to talk about real-world model deployment, not just textbook theory.
core_philosophy: Employers don't just want to see a high accuracy metric. They want to know how you handled missing values and how you put that model into a live environment. This layout bridges the gap between Kaggle and corporate engineering.
personal_story: During our research, a Senior Data Scientist told us exactly why he rejects junior applicants. He said, 'Real world data is messy. Where is the mess in their resume?' The candidates who get hired are the ones who focus on how they handled dirty data and severe model overfitting, rather than just showing a perfect 99% accuracy score.
ats_optimizations: We balanced the machine learning terms with basic statistical forecasting words so you satisfy both the HR scanners and Lead Engineers.
We highlighted data preparation right next to model tuning so you look like a comprehensive full-stack data scientist.
We formatted the GitHub and Kaggle links so the ATS bots actually register them as valid portfolio artifacts.
We prioritized feature engineering over simple algorithm name-dropping to show you have deep domain knowledge.

title: Machine Learning Engineer
card_description: Targeted ATS templates packed with power words for model deployment, NLP, deep learning, and MLOps.
description: Our research shows that an ML model that only works on a local Jupyter notebook is completely useless to a company. Companies need engineers who can deploy to the cloud. We built this template to highlight your MLOps architecture.
core_philosophy: We shifted the focus of this resume away from raw math and heavily into endpoint structuring and Docker containerization. If you can't prove you understand inferencing speed and cloud deployment, you won't pass the technical screen.
personal_story: We analyzed the trajectory of successful ML Engineers and found a turning point in their careers. Their early resumes focused entirely on math, which got ignored. They started getting interviews the moment they rewrote their resumes to focus on deployment—like how an AI model was too slow for a mobile app, and how they wrapped it in a Docker container to reduce latency.
ats_optimizations: We front-loaded the neural network architectures so you hit the high-tier specialization filters immediately.
We put your cloud platform integration skills right next to your modeling projects to satisfy our cross-disciplinary requirements.
We structured the bullet points so you have to show exact model accuracy improvements over time.
We injected specific MLOps terminology that I rarely see on junior resumes to instantly elevate your profile.

title: Business Analyst
card_description: Communicate stakeholder engagement, requirement gathering, and process optimization strictly in ATS-friendly language.
description: A Business Analyst who can't translate technical requirements into executive summaries is a massive liability. Our team designed this template to bridge the gap between your SQL queries and actual human communication.
core_philosophy: This format ensures your hard technical skills are tied directly to words like 'Stakeholder Engagement'. It is highly optimized for the heavily regulated industries we researched, like banking and healthcare IT.
personal_story: We researched the difference between junior and senior business analysts. The juniors write 'Gathered Requirements' on their resume. The seniors tell a story: they explain how a team was manually approving 500 invoices a month, causing huge delays, and how their AS-IS process map cut time by 75%. You have to show the human error you encountered and the exact workflow you designed to fix it.
ats_optimizations: We injected Agile and Scrum language throughout the document because our project management sweeps demand it.
We grouped the mapping and visualization tools together to hit the standard keyword density checks used by Fortune 500 banks.
We forced a clean, readable layout that appeals to non-technical HR managers while keeping enough tech terms for the IT directors.
We added phrasing that highlights your cross-functional team coordination, proving you can lead without formal authority.

title: AI Engineer / GenAI
card_description: Modernized templates with prompt engineering, LLM integration, and generative AI keywords formatted for robots.
description: Generative AI is a fundamentally different field, so using a standard 2020 software resume makes you look completely outdated. We built this explicitly to prove you understand prompt optimization and token limits.
core_philosophy: Startups hiring AI engineers right now only care about two things: RAG architectures and API cost reduction. This template isolates your Large Language Model fine-tuning skills and forces you to explain your token optimization strategies.
personal_story: We analyzed the hiring boom in Generative AI. At first, everyone's resume looked identical: 'Used OpenAI API.' The candidates who actually landed jobs were the ones who detailed a specific project where the LLM hallucinated, and exactly how they architected a RAG pipeline to force semantic search and eliminate the hallucinations. You have to prove you understand the limitations of the technology.
ats_optimizations: We packed this densely with the new 2026 ATS keywords dealing specifically with generative tech and latent space methodologies.
We highlighted vector databases naturally within standard software pipelines to prove your architectural competence.
We clearly separated your foundational ML knowledge from your modern generative API skills so I can verify your technological timeline.
We emphasized cost-reduction techniques in API calling, which is my number one priority when hiring.

title: Cloud Engineer
card_description: Pre-populated with essential power phrases for AWS/Azure/GCP architecture, CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure as code.
description: If a cloud resume focuses entirely on basic IT support tasks, it gets rejected immediately. Employers need to know you can handle highly scalable, secure infrastructure. We formatted this to highlight your continuous integration skills.
core_philosophy: Employers want to see your CI/CD pipelines right next to your AWS certifications. This layout walks you through framing simple university web-hosting projects as 'High-Availability Cloud Architecture Implementations.'
personal_story: We spoke with cloud recruiters, and they told us that AWS certifications alone don't guarantee a job. What guarantees a job is a resume that tells a story about downtime. The best applicants write about how manual server deployments caused 30 minutes of downtime, and how they used Terraform to automate a CI/CD pipeline to achieve 99% uptime.
ats_optimizations: We clustered the CI/CD automation tools directly next to major cloud platform names to trigger our exact-match parameters.
We built a dedicated block for cloud certifications, which are mandatory for many of the automated ATS gateways we use.
We highlighted deep Linux administration and basic bash scripting organically within the project descriptions.
We framed simple web-hosting projects as high-availability implementations to maximize your authority score.

title: Power BI Developer
card_description: Purpose-built for BI specialists who need to prove dashboard design, DAX mastery, and enterprise data modeling skills to ATS systems.
description: Most Power BI resumes get rejected because they just say 'I built dashboards.' Companies don't need a dashboard builder; they need a full-stack BI professional. This template forces you to prove you own the entire data pipeline.
core_philosophy: Employers strictly look for outcome-driven language. 'Reduced reporting cycle from 5 days to 4 hours' beats 'Experienced with DAX' every single time. This layout heavily separates Power Query from DAX to prove deep ecosystem knowledge.
personal_story: When we researched enterprise BI hiring, we saw a hundred resumes that just said 'Created visual dashboards.' They all got rejected. The resumes that won the job focused on performance bottlenecks—like when data refresh rates were taking 6 hours, and how the candidate rewrote the underlying DAX calculations to bring it down to 15 minutes.
ats_optimizations: We structured the skills into Data Modeling, DAX, and Visualization so our ATS parsers register your deep BI specialization.
We injected Power Platform ecosystem keywords because they are increasingly mandatory for my enterprise Microsoft environment roles.
We formatted the project descriptions to highlight Row-Level Security, an advanced keyword I rarely find on junior BI resumes.
We included explicit mention of data source connectors to satisfy both our cloud-native and on-premise job filters.
